record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Develop a theory of chiral covers of polytopes: define the right notion of quotient and cover in the chiral setting, and formulate the analogue of the regular-cover theory for chiral polytopes.

evidence.quote: Problem 5 Develop a theory of chiral covers of polytopes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank $n$ is a partially ordered set $\mathcal{P}$, with a strictly monotone rank function onto $\{-1,0,1,\dots,n\}$, satisfying: (i) $\mathcal{P}$ has a unique minimum face (of rank $-1$) and a unique maximum face (of rank $n$); (ii) every maximal chain (flag) has exactly $n+2$ elements; (iii) $\mathcal{P}$ is strongly flag-connected; and (iv) the diamond condition: whenever $F < G$ with $\mathrm{rank}(G)-\mathrm{rank}(F)=2$, there are exactly two faces strictly between $F$ and $G$. An automorphism of $\mathcal{P}$ is an order-preserving bijection. The polytope $\mathcal{P}$ is called regular if its automorphism group acts transitively on flags, and chiral if its automorphism group has exactly two orbits on flags such that adjacent flags lie in different orbits.

Given two abstract polytopes $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ of the same rank, $\mathcal{P}$ is said to cover $\mathcal{Q}$ if there exists a surjection $\mathcal{P} \to \mathcal{Q}$ which preserves rank, incidence, and adjacency of flags; one then says $\mathcal{Q}$ is a quotient of $\mathcal{P}$. For regular polytopes, there is a well-developed theory in which quotients correspond to certain normal subgroups of the automorphism group of the universal regular polytope of a given Schläfli type.

Develop the analogous theory of covers and quotients in the chiral setting. Specifically:
(a) Formulate the appropriate notions of "chiral cover" and "chiral quotient" between chiral polytopes (and possibly between chiral and regular polytopes), accounting for the role of the two flag orbits and the handedness (mirror image) of chiral polytopes.
(b) Give a group-theoretic characterization of chiral covers in terms of the rotation subgroups (or their analogues) of the automorphism groups, identifying which subgroups give rise to chiral quotients that are again polytopes.
(c) Establish the analogue, in the chiral setting, of the regular-cover theory: in particular, describe a universal chiral polytope of a prescribed Schläfli type from which all chiral polytopes of that type arise as quotients, and characterize the corresponding covering relations.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial progress has been made on aspects of chiral covers since the problem was posed. Notable contributions include work on abelian covers of chiral polytopes (Cunningham–Pellicer, J. Algebra 2017), chiral extensions of chiral polytopes (Cunningham–Pellicer), and the study of chiral polytopes whose smallest regular cover is itself a polytope (J. Combin. Theory Ser. A, 2024). However, a complete general theory of chiral covers and quotients fully analogous to the regular-cover theory does not appear to have been established in the literature, so the program as a whole remains open.

status_evidence.title: Abelian covers of chiral polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Cunningham and Pellicer develop a theory of abelian covers in the chiral setting.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on the cover theory for chiral polytopes via abelian covers.

status_evidence.title: Chiral polytopes whose smallest regular cover is a polytope
status_evidence.snippet: Studies when the smallest regular cover of a chiral polytope is itself a polytope.
status_evidence.claim: Recent results on regular covers of chiral polytopes indicate ongoing partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Chiral extensions of chiral polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Cunningham–Pellicer construct chiral (d+1)-polytopes with chiral facets, contributing to the covers/extensions theory.
status_evidence.claim: Extension/cover constructions in the chiral setting have been partially developed.
